sources.entry: Transmission Remote GUI - Native SwiftUI remote for the Transmission daemon with torrent rules, RSS auto-download and tracker/folder filters; a modern transgui alternative.

summary.one_liner: A native SwiftUI macOS remote GUI for the Transmission BitTorrent daemon, speaking its RPC protocol, intended as a modern alternative to transgui.
summary.what_it_does: It connects to one or more Transmission daemons and shows a sortable, customizable torrent list with sidebar filters by status, tracker, download folder and label. Torrents can be added by magnet link, .torrent file or drag and drop, with a per-torrent download folder. A details panel covers General, Files (folder tree), Peers (with country flags) and Trackers, and torrent rules set ratio, idle limits, speed limits or labels per tracker, label or name, with a dry run before applying. An RSS auto-downloader with title-match rules, session settings, turtle mode with a bandwidth scheduler, and a menu bar icon with speed graph are also included. The UI is available in English, Hungarian and Simplified Chinese.
use_cases: Manage a remote Transmission daemon from a Mac
Add torrents to a server by magnet link or .torrent file
Automatically download torrents from RSS feeds
Set seed ratio or speed limits per tracker
Monitor transfer speeds from the menu bar
how_to_run: ./Scripts/build-app.sh # builds dist/Transmission Remote GUI.app (release build, ad-hoc signed)
swift run TransmissionRemoteGUI # run for development
transmission-daemon --foreground --port 9091 # test daemon, then add 127.0.0.1:9091 in Settings → Servers
notable: Clean-room Swift reimplementation of the transgui features, with no code from other projects
Torrent rules engine: first match wins, each torrent classified once, dry run before changes, and ratio/idle limits enforced by the daemon while the app is closed
Peer country flags from a bundled offline DB-IP table, with no peer addresses sent anywhere
Optional mTLS client-certificate authentication per server
Opt-in anonymous usage statistics, off by default
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later; Linux and Windows are not mentioned
Ad-hoc signed only; distributing to other Macs requires an Apple Developer ID and notarization
Roadmap items still open include queue reordering, tracker add/remove, watch folder and JSON-RPC 2.0 support
keywords: control torrents on server from mac
